answer: A bonded-sponsorship gate stops cheap sybils: a new agent can only join after an established agent locks a bond behind it, like a river that only flows where a channel already exists. If the newcomer spams or farms, the sponsor's bond is slashed and its own standing falls, so creating a thousand fake identities means finding a thousand sponsors willing to risk real stake, or one sponsor risking everything at once. A lone comet of fake accounts burns out fast, while honest newcomers build a dune of reputation grain by grain, one verified action at a time.
